findings.message: The round-1 finding is only partly fixed. `history` lists only commits that touch the covered change's own `.specclaw/changes/<name>` directory. Code commits for a change usually touch `modules/…` and nothing under its change directory, so `loopProblem` never sees them. A code commit made after the covering loop's final pass therefore goes unreviewed and still passes. The `between` test only fails because its late commit also writes `103-stacked/notes.md`. Fix: check every commit in `base..head` that is not an ancestor of the cover's final head. Every such commit that touches anything outside `.specclaw/` must be owned by a self-reviewed change in the PR. Add a test case with a code-only late commit.
findings.scenario: Fork branch: `stacked`, then `reviewed` (101-cover's final pass at that head, Verify names 103-stacked), then a commit `specclaw(103-stacked): more code` that touches only `modules/demo/c.ts`. Result: `103-stacked scope=covered-by pass`, but 101-cover's loop never saw c.ts.

findings.message: `ownedElsewhere` excuses a late commit on its subject line alone. It only checks that the subject names some other self-reviewed change in the PR. It never checks that the other change's loop reviewed that commit, i.e. that the owner's final head descends from the commit. `judgeEvidence` only asks that the owner's final head is in the PR, so neither loop ever saw the commit. On a fork PR the subject is text the contributor chooses. Fix: excuse the commit only when `isAncestor(commit.sha, finalRound(owner.rounds).head)`. Add a test where the owner's final pass comes before the excused commit; that case must fail.
findings.scenario: Fork branch: `stacked`, `reviewed`, then 105-other with a clean final round at that head, then a commit `[specclaw] 105-other: x` that edits `modules/demo/c.ts` and `103-stacked/notes.md`. Both 103-stacked and 105-other pass, and the commit was reviewed by no loop.

findings.message: `verifySection` takes the first `indexOf("## Verify")` anywhere in the file. That can be a prose mention, for example 078's own change.md line 8 "(073 `## Verify`)" or 074's AC text. The new `split(/^## (?!Verify)/m)` then ends the section at the next heading, so the real `## Verify` is never read. The covered-by name check and the blocker-stop check both read the wrong text. They fail a correct cover, or pass when the prose near the mention happens to name the change. Fix: anchor the match to a heading line (`/^## Verify[ \t]*$/m`). Add test cases where the cover's change.md mentions `## Verify` in its Problem text.
findings.scenario: 101-cover's change.md says "See 103-stacked under `## Verify` later" in ## Problem, and its real ## Verify names nothing. The gate passes the 'names 103-stacked' check. The reverse case: real Verify names 103-stacked, the prose mention does not → `101-cover's ## Verify doesn't name 103-stacked`.

findings.message: `commit()` ignores `git show`'s exit status and decides `recordsOnly` with `paths.every(...)`. An empty path list therefore reads as 'records only'. That covers a `git show` that failed (missing object in a shallow or partial clone) and a clean merge commit, whose `--cc --name-only` output lists no files. Either way a late commit is excused as records-only instead of being reported as unknown. `history` also ignores `rev-list`'s status, so a failure there produces the misleading `final pass ran before any … commit`. Fix: throw on a non-zero status, as `inBase` does. Treat an empty path list as not records-only, and list merge files with `-m --first-parent` or `--diff-merges=first-parent`.
findings.scenario: After the cover's final pass, the fork merges a side branch that edits 103-stacked's files without conflict. `git show --name-only` on the merge prints only the subject, so `recordsOnly` is true and 103-stacked passes.

findings.message: `names()` puts `name` into a `RegExp` without escaping it. `CHANGE_DIR` accepts any `\d{3}-[^/]+`, so a dir like `103-a.b` makes `.` match any character, and `103-x(` makes the constructor throw and crash the gate. Escape the name, or compare against `[\w-]` tokens.
findings.scenario: A change dir `103-a.b`, and the cover's Verify says `103-aXb` → the name check passes.

findings.message: This 078 diff still adds mock sections and amendments for 070–077 (074-dev-demo-data, 075, 076, 077, 073 amendment 1, 070 amendments 2–5) alongside 078's own section. Each change owns its own `<section data-change>`. Keep 078's edit to its own section, or list the others in 078's Mock Delta.

[design] This fixes only the named case. `history(change.name)` runs `rev-list` limited to `.specclaw/changes/<name>` and `archive/<name>`, so the after-final-pass check only sees commits that also touch the change's records dir. AGENTS.md now says that a commit to the change after the final pass must touch only `.specclaw/`. A code-only commit for the covered change never touches its dir, so the gate never sees it. The `between` test passes only because its planted commit edits `103-stacked/notes.md` as well as `modules/demo/c.ts`. Fix: attribute commits to the change by their subject as well as by path. Every commit in `base..head` whose subject names the covered change (`specclaw(<name>)` / `[specclaw] <name>`), or that touches its dir, must be an ancestor of the cover's final head or be records-only. Add a test with a code-only `specclaw(103-stacked)` commit after the cover's final pass, and assert it fails.
findings.scenario: Fork PR: 103-stacked is covered-by 101-cover. 101-cover's final round is clean at H. A later commit `specclaw(103-stacked): more code` changes only `modules/demo/c.ts`. history('103-stacked') leaves it out, so `later` is empty and the gate prints `103-stacked scope=covered-by pass`. The new code was never reviewed.
